previous_task_text:
## Scientific question

Starting from the supplied cyclic oxocarbenium ions and triarylborohydride anions, explain catalyst-dependent cis/trans formation selectivity in the local reduction stage of hydrogenative reductive cycloetherification of D4 (1,4-diphenylbutane-1,4-dione) and D5 (1,5-diphenylpentane-1,5-dione), and its relation to product stability across ring sizes. Account for the supplied triarylborane performance comparisons using molecular evidence. This is an explanation task; the measured ratios and yields are supplied observations.

## Input files

`data/inputs/system.json` supplies molecular identities and cis/trans definitions (PI1), reaction conditions (PI2), and the observation matrix (PI3). A repeated terminal O in a ring description indicates the same ring-closing atom. Catalyst A is B(C6F5)3; B and C have the distinct specified aryl substitution patterns. `data/inputs/local_reduction_structures.json` and the corresponding SDF files define the D4/D5 oxocarbenium ions (+1, singlet) and A/B borohydrides (-1, singlet), together with A/B/C borane graphs. Oxonium and carbon-centered resonance drawings describe the same delocalized cation. The chosen single stereocentre in each cation is an arbitrary enantiomer for modeling cis/trans competition; no experimental enantiopurity is implied. SDF coordinates are two-dimensional depictions. `submission_schema.json` and `submission_guide.md` specify the output contract.

## Scope

Compare hydride delivery to the supplied D4 cation by A/B borohydrides, and D4 versus D5 cations with A fixed. Formation of these local reactants from diketones, H2 cleavage and catalyst regeneration are outside the required scope. Use a common, balanced cation-plus-borohydride or justified associated-pair reference for each formation competition; neutral products include the returned borane. The K4 screen with A/B/C provides context for catalyst function; it does not require calculating furan pathways or endpoint yields. Preserve the distinct D4/D5 conditions (80 °C, CPME) and K4 screen (50 °C, diisopropyl ether), each under 100 bar H2 for 18 h. Keep isolated and NMR yields, ratios and lower bounds distinct. Choose and justify reactive states, molecular models, charge/spin and computational methods. A complete catalytic network, unlisted catalyst/substrate pairs, quantitative turnover, pressure dependence and solvent-screen mechanisms are outside scope.

## Required results

1. Give a computed molecular account of the three catalysts' relevant behavior and explain what it establishes about the performance screen. Report quantitative comparisons with their physical definitions; distinguish affinity, activation and endpoint conversion.
2. Explain D4 cis enrichment for both A and B using competing formation calculations and independent product stability. Report the formation and product free-energy differences.
3. Quantify how the A-to-B substitution changes D4 stereochemical discrimination and assess the strength and robustness of the calculated contrast.
4. With A fixed, explain the D4/D5 ring-size effect on formation preference and product stability, reporting both types of free-energy differences and their physical origin.

Choose your own hypotheses and competing hydride-delivery geometries within this local starting boundary. Verify states, reaction connectivity and numerical definitions to the extent needed for the claims. No specific intermediate sequence, descriptor, transition-state count or exhaustive conformer search is prescribed. Separate formation barriers from product free energies, and disclose low-frequency and conformational sensitivity where material. Repeating the observations does not supply computational evidence.

Continue the research until you reach the final conclusions.

## Submission and permitted resources

Submit `report/results.json`, `report/report.md` and real input/output/log/analysis files under `research/`, linked through the existing schema. Use the supplied public inputs and independently generated calculations with chosen software. Report actual resource use, evidence-supported conclusions and remaining uncertainty; preserve failed attempts. Scientific credit is assigned only to final supported outcomes, totaling 100 points, without process points.
previous_submission_guide_text:
# Submission guide

Submit `report/results.json`, `report/report.md`, and the actual inputs, outputs,
logs and analysis code under `research/`. Follow `submission_schema.json`.

Use stable IDs for hypotheses, investigations, evidence and conclusions. Every
evidence investigation ID and every conclusion evidence ID must resolve to a
submitted record. Refer to real files with safe relative paths; absolute paths,
parent-directory traversal and symlinks escaping the submission are forbidden.
List each referenced artifact in reproducibility.artifact_index. Preserve object,
state and unit mappings. Numerical evidence includes its definition, units and
conditions; use null with an explanation when a value is unavailable.

For each investigation record a brief purpose, chosen method, actual outcome and
any resulting decision. Do not provide private chain of thought. No fixed number
of hypotheses or tests is required. Requirements for stationary points, kinetics
or other model checks follow the claims actually made.

Research status is complete, partial or execution_failed. Question status is
resolved, partially_resolved or unresolved. These describe different things:
careful research can leave a question unresolved. Complete or resolved claims
require completed investigations, evidence and linked conclusions; a status label
alone establishes nothing. Failed work must include attempted inputs, error logs
and an explanation; do not invent missing results. No fixed scientific compute
quota is imposed. Report actual resource use in the readable report.

Scientific credit is awarded only for independently supported final outcomes, totaling 100 points. There is no separate process or research-quality score. A supported equivalent scientific explanation can pass; missing or unsupported conclusions fail.
Schema acceptance checks structure and does not certify scientific completion.

Choose your own hypotheses, computational models and research approach.
